note: toc_api_example is a one-hook reference implementation of the TOC API. hook_node_view() adds a TOC to 'page' and 'article' nodes in the 'full' view mode when the body has >= header_count (default 2) top-level headers, using the 'default' toc_type's options and the toc_api.manager/toc_api.builder services. No config, routes, or permissions of its own. Medium cases read the live 'default' toc_type (title/template) that the demo relies on (setup mutates it, cleanup restores the shipped values title='Table of Contents', template='responsive'). Hard cases create an Article/Page node whose multi-heading body makes the demo render a TOC, verified by rendering the node full view and detecting the toc-responsive wrapper; reset deletes the node so verify fails on empty state.

evals.prompt: In the toc_api_example module, which Drupal hook is used to inject a table of contents into rendered nodes?
evals.expected_output: It implements hook_node_view() (toc_api_example_node_view()), which alters the node's build render array to prepend a TOC.

evals.prompt: Which content types and which view mode does toc_api_example add a table of contents to?
evals.expected_output: Page and Article nodes, in the 'full' view mode (and only when a body field is present).

evals.prompt: toc_api_example doesn't always show a table of contents. What condition decides whether the TOC actually appears on a node?
evals.expected_output: It only replaces the body when $toc->isVisible() is true — i.e. the body contains at least header_count (default 2) top-level headers.

evals.prompt: toc_api_example builds its table of contents from the 'default' TOC API type. Inspect the live configuration and tell me the table-of-contents title currently set on that type.
evals.expected_output: The title is 'Eval Page Contents': toc_api.toc_type.default has options.title = 'Eval Page Contents' (drush cget toc_api.toc_type.default options.title).

evals.prompt: The demo module renders its TOC using the 'default' TOC API type. Look at that type's live configuration and state which table-of-contents template (layout) it currently uses.
evals.expected_output: The 'tree' template: toc_api.toc_type.default has options.template = tree.

evals.prompt: The toc_api_example module is enabled on this site. Create an Article node titled exactly 'TOC Api Example Article' whose body contains at least three HTML h2 headings (use a full-HTML text format), so that when the node is viewed the module automatically renders a table of contents. Save it to the live site.
evals.expected_output: An Article node 'TOC Api Example Article' exists whose body (full_html) contains multiple <h2> headings, so that parsing the body with the 'default' toc_type yields a visible TOC (TocInterface::isVisible() is true, i.e. >= header_count top-level headers) — exactly the precondition toc_api_example_node_view() uses before replacing the body.

evals.prompt: I have the TOC API example module turned on. Write a blog-style Article titled exactly 'TOC Api Example Blog' with a few big section headings in its body so the article automatically shows a clickable table of contents at the top. Publish it on the site.
evals.expected_output: An Article node 'TOC Api Example Blog' exists whose body (full_html) has multiple <h2> headings, so parsing it with the 'default' toc_type produces a visible TOC (TocInterface::isVisible() true) — the precondition toc_api_example uses before injecting a TOC into page/article bodies. (Note: on a standard site this also works for the 'page' type, but this site's Page bundle has no body field.)
